## PDF page 226

[Open source PDF](../../../../sources/pdf/GTO/Poker-Math-Preflop-Workbook.pdf#page=226)

```text
                             CHAPTER EIGHTEEN



              GOING ALL-IN PREFLOP


Is there anything more exciting than a big all-in preflop? What most players
fail to realize is that these all-ins are incredibly mathematical. And while you
will not pull out Flopzilla and a calculator in the middle of a hand to proof
the math – by doing these kinds of exercises you will be able to more closely
estimate if calling all-ins rate to make or lose you money at the table.

This work ties together a variety of the skills we have already explored. Con-
cepts like EV, hand vs. range equities, blockers, and pot odds all come into
play. In real-time you will also be responsible for building your opponent’s
all-in range, but the good news is that many players use similar ranges.

So take your time working through each calculation and over time you will
build an intuition for making +EV decisions when facing all-ins.

Each of these exercises is going to lay out a preflop situation and an
assumed all-in range for your opponent. You will then calculate the EV of
calling that all-in with a few different starting hands. This will allow you to get
more practice and better understand how different hands perform in these
scenarios.

TOOLS TO USE: Most players should do these exercises with pen & paper. If
you would like to use a tool, download and use my “Basic EV” spreadsheet
available at www.splitsuit.pro/sheets

                                    PA G E 2 2 6
```

## PDF page 227

[Open source PDF](../../../../sources/pdf/GTO/Poker-Math-Preflop-Workbook.pdf#page=227)

```text
                         GOING ALL-IN PREFLOP: CALLS


PROCESS: Read the prompt and discern the key information. Begin with the
first starting hand and calculate the equity of that hand against their range.

Next, fill in each variable in the formula to the side and calculate the EV.




Repeat this process for the other starting hands.

TAKEAWAYS: When facing these preflop all-ins, you have two options: call
or fold. In general, if a call is +EV, you should call. If a call is -EV, you should
fold. Just know that there are tournament-specific factors that can make it
correct to fold even +EV hands. For example, you would always call a preflop
all-in with AA in a cash game. But in a satellite, even though calling that
preflop all-in would be +EV with AA, it could be correct to fold.

Notice which hands perform best in these scenarios, and also note any spot
where it is +EV to call with weaker hole cards. We do these kinds of exercises
so that we stay focused on the pot odds, equities, and EV to avoid making
incorrect folds solely because our hole cards are not perfect.

GLGL.

                                     PA G E 2 2 7
```
